QQQI pays 13.6% versus JEPQ's 11.3%, but both funds cap upside by selling covered calls on the Nasdaq-100.

QQQ gained 23% last year while QQQI and JEPQ returned only 18% and 19%, proving the call overlay costs real upside in bull markets.

QQQI classified between 94 and 99 percent of its distributions as return of capital, deferring taxes for long-term taxable holders but delivering no edge inside an IRA.

Building a portfolio and living off one are two completely different skills, and almost nobody teaches the second. This problem is what The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income helps, and it is free today. Read more here. (Sponsor)

NEOS Nasdaq-100 High Income ETF (NASDAQ:QQQI) carries a trailing 12-month distribution yield of 13.6%, measured against its October 9, 2026 close. The better-known JPMorgan Nasdaq Equity Premium Income ETF (NASDAQ:JEPQ) yields 11.3% on the same basis. Both pay 12 times a year, and both sell calls on the Nasdaq-100. So if the lesser-known fund pays more, why would anyone own the other one?

Arsenii Palivoda / Shutterstock.com

Start with what those figures are. Each one divides the past year's distributions by the share price, so it shows the past. Both are backward-looking payout measures. On forward annualized payouts, the two land at 13.5% and 11.1%, which looks a lot like the trailing numbers. Option income rises and falls with market volatility, and the checks move with it. JEPQ's latest payment was $0.57, down from $0.68 the month before.

Two Different Machines Generate These Payouts

Both funds rely on a covered call strategy. That means that they own stocks and sell someone the right to buy them at a set price by a set date. The buyer pays an upfront fee, called the option premium, and that premium funds the distribution. In exchange, any gains above the agreed price go to the buyer.

JEPQ runs an actively managed stock portfolio selected from the Nasdaq-100, led by NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) at 7%, with the next-largest position at 6%. It gets its option income indirectly, through equity-linked notes. These are bank-issued debt securities with a short Nasdaq-100 call built in, and they pass the premium back as coupons. Its June filing lists notes from BNP Paribas and other large banks, each worth roughly 1% of net assets. The fund takes on exposure to those banks, and note coupons generally reach shareholders as ordinary income.

title: The Compounding Catch: How TQQQ’s 3x Daily Target Became a 5.93x Windfall
detail:
The Compounding Catch: How TQQQ’s 3x Daily Target Became a 5.93x Windfall
Ryne Mauck
Mon, October 12, 2026 at 1:03 PM PDT 5 min read
TQQQ
QLD
QQQ
Explore stocks on Coinbase

Quick Read

TQQQ's 3x daily leverage compounded into a 5.93x ten-year multiple of QQQ, turning a 539% index gain into a 3,197% return.

Over five years, triple-leverage TQQQ (168%) nearly matched double-leverage QLD (169%), showing high volatility can erase an entire unit of leverage.

TQQQ lost 79% in 2022 alone, and a single 33% down day in the index could wipe out holders entirely.

Building a portfolio and living off one are two completely different skills, and almost nobody teaches the second. This problem is what The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income helps, and it is free today. Read more here. (Sponsor)

Over the past ten years, the ProShares UltraPro QQQ (NASDAQ:TQQQ) posted a price return of 3197.28%. The ProShares Ultra QQQ (NYSEARCA:QLD) returned 1788.39%, and the plain Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) returned 539.27%. All three figures run through the October 9, 2026 close. All three funds target the same Nasdaq-100 Index, but in very different ways.

bigjom jom / Shutterstock.com
Two of These Funds Only Promise One Day at a Time

ProShares says TQQQ seeks daily results, before fees and expenses, equal to three times (3x) the Nasdaq-100's daily performance, and ProShares sets QLD's target at two times (2x) the index's daily move. ProShares' TQQQ prospectus spells out the limit: "The Fund does not seek to achieve three times (3x) the daily performance of the Index ... for any period other than a day." The QLD document contains the same sentence for its 2x target.

Anyone buying either fund expecting a multiple of the index's long-run return has misunderstood the product.

Both funds hold Nasdaq-100 stocks alongside derivative positions, Treasury securities, repurchase agreements (short-term secured loans) and a stake in the ProShares GENIUS Money Market ETF, according to their May 31, 2026 holdings reports. The derivatives include swap agreements and futures contracts.

Each day the fund rebalances, resetting exposure to its daily target. When the index rises, the fund must add exposure. When it falls, the fund must cut exposure. That mechanism is why multi-day results drift from the multiple.

In this episode of ETF Spotlight, I speak with Christopher Dahlin, Invesco's Senior Factor & Core Equity Strategist, about the AI trade, equal-weighted strategies, and factor investing.

The AI trade came roaring back over the past few weeks. The Magnificent Seven's combined market capitalization topped $25 trillion during last Tuesday's trading session, while NVIDIA NVDA, the AI darling, is on track to become the first company ever to reach a $6 trillion valuation.

Investors appear to be treating mega-cap technology stocks as safe havens once again amid rising uncertainty surrounding the upcoming midterm elections, the ongoing war in the Middle East, and elevated interest rates.

The Nasdaq-100 Index is one of the most effective ways to play the AI rally, as it provides exposure to some of the most innovative companies leveraging AI. The Invesco QQQ ETF QQQ and its cheaper counterpart, the Invesco NASDAQ 100 ETF QQQM, have returned more than 175% since bottoming in October 2022.

BlackRock and State Street have also launched their own ETFs tracking the Nasdaq-100. NVIDIA, Apple AAPL, Microsoft MSFT, and Micron MU account for more than 26% of the portfolios of these ETFs.

While mega-cap stocks continue to perform well, there's still a lot of interest in equal-weighted strategies. The Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF RSP recently reached $100 billion in assets under management (AUM), suggesting that some investors have become concerned about concentration in the indexes.

The top 10 holdings now account for about 40% of the S&P 500, while the information technology and communication services sectors together make up almost half of the index and are dominated by AI-related names.

Momentum and high beta have been the strongest U.S. equity factors this year, while low volatility, dividend yield, and size have lagged. Factor returns are cyclical, and it's always difficult to predict market timing and factor cycles. How should investors incorporate factors into their portfolios?

Generating $4,300/month from JEPQ requires roughly $469,000 (7,674 shares) at the fund's current 11.1% distribution rate.

Monthly payouts vary widely, and 7,674 shares produced as little as $2,607 in low months, so retirees should budget around $3,574, not $4,300.

JEPQ is non-diversified, trails QQQ in bull markets, and concentrates 27% of holdings in a handful of tech and chip stocks.

Building a portfolio and living off one are two completely different skills, and almost nobody teaches the second. This problem is what The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income helps, and it is free today. Read more here. (Sponsor)

Some retirees are drawn to the simplest income plan imaginable: put everything into a single fund that pays monthly. For a 72-year-old, that would mean one holding, one statement, one deposit, and nothing to rebalance. So let's see what it would actually take to do that with the JPMorgan Nasdaq Equity Premium Income ETF (NASDAQ:JEPQ). The goal is $4,300 a month, or $51,600 a year, with JEPQ making up 100% of the portfolio.

zah108 / Shutterstock.com

JEPQ's payout changes monthly by design, so a retiree should plan for how much the $4,300 will swing.

Where JEPQ's Monthly Check Comes From

JEPQ holds a portfolio of stocks drawn largely from the Nasdaq-100. The fund also sells call options on that index through equity-linked notes (ELNs), which are bank-issued securities that package the option income. Selling a call means the fund gives a buyer the right to purchase at a set price and makes a payment, called premium, for that right.

Premium pays the most when markets are jumpy and shrinks when they're calm. The VIX, a measure of expected stock volatility, read 15 in early October, which falls in its normal range. JEPQ's payout rate tracks market conditions, so it acts less like a conventional dividend yield.

T. Rowe Price yields 4.93% backed by $3.23 billion in cash, while Franklin Templeton pairs a 4.04% yield with record $1.8 trillion AUM and positive net inflows.

BlackRock trades a modest 2.05% yield for the group's strongest dividend growth, raising its quarterly payout from $0.78 in 2009 to $5.73 today, including a recent 10% increase.

Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now, and T. Rowe Price didn't make the cut. Enter your email to see the names that beat TROW. The report is free. Enter your email and see if any of your stocks made the cut.

Asset managers make money in a simple way. They charge a small annual fee on every dollar of client money they manage, which the industry calls assets under management, or AUM. AUM grows two ways: markets go up, or clients put in more money than they take out (net inflows), and it shrinks when markets fall or when clients withdraw (net outflows). The dividend depends on market levels and client behavior.

Panchenko Vladimir / Shutterstock.com

There is no product cycle or regulated rate base behind it, so these stocks pay income differently from an industrial or a utility. Right now the background is strong: industry leader BlackRock (NYSE:BLK) ended its latest quarter with a record $15.3 trillion in AUM. All four names below run on the same fee engine, but their yields are far apart, and the lowest yielder makes the list because its payout grows reliably, while the others make it on the size of their checks.

title: Exchange-Traded Funds Lower, Equity Futures Mixed Pre-Bell Monday as Investors Weigh Oil, Earnings
detail:
PREMIUM
Exchange-Traded Funds Lower, Equity Futures Mixed Pre-Bell Monday as Investors Weigh Oil, Earnings
MT Newswires
Mon, October 12, 2026 at 6:00 AM PDT 3 min read
BTC-USD
^GSPC
^DJI
^IXIC
XLE
Trade BTC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The broad market exchange-traded fund SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) was up 0.03%, and the actively traded Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) retreated 0.2% in Monday's premarket activity, as investors monitored Middle East tensions, oil prices, and the start of quarterly earnings.

US stock futures were mixed, with S&P 500 Index futures marginally higher, Dow Jones Industrial Average futures gaining 0.1%, and Nasdaq futures slipping 0.2% before the start of regular trading.

In premarket action, bitcoin was down by 0.4%. Among cryptocurrency ETFs, the cryptocurrency fund ProShares Bitcoin Strategy ETF (BITO) was 1% higher, Ether ETF (EETH) advanced 2.6%, and Bitcoin & Ether Market Cap Weight ETF (BETH) was flat.

Power Play:

Energy

The iShares US Energy ETF (IYE) gained 0.2%, while the State Street Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLE) was up by 1%.

DHT (DHT) shares were up 4% after the company said it expects time charter equivalent earnings of $141,300 per day for its fleet in Q3.

Winners and Losers:

Financial

The State Street Financial Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLF) advanced 0.2%. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X Shares (FAS) was up 0.7%, while its bearish counterpart, Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X Shares (FAZ), was 0.3% lower.

IREN (IREN) shares were up more than 3% following a report by The Information revealing that Anthropic is the unnamed "frontier AI lab" in its major cloud services contract that co-CEO Daniel Roberts referenced in IREN's fiscal Q4 earnings call in August.

Industrial

The State Street Industrial Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLI) fell 0.1%, while the Vanguard Industrials Index Fund (VIS) and the iShares US Industrials ETF (IYJ) were inactive.

Hub Group (HUBG) stock was up more than 3% before the opening bell after Baird upgraded the company to outperform.

Technology

The State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) retreated 0.3%, the iShares US Technology ETF (IYW) was 0.2% higher, and the iShares Expanded Tech Sector ETF (IGM) was inactive. Among semiconductor ETFs, the State Street SPDR S&P Semiconductor ETF (XSD) was down 0.9%, while the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) fell by 1.1%.

Salesforce (CRM) shares were up more than 3% in premarket activity after BofA Securities upgraded the company to buy from underperform.

Consumer

The State Street Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLP) was up 0.1%, the Vanguard Consumer Staples Index Fund ETF Shares (VDC), the iShares US Consumer Staples ETF (IYK), the State Street Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLY), the VanEck Retail ETF (RTH) and the State Street SPDR S&P Retail ETF (XRT) were inactive.

Stellantis (STLA) shares were up nearly 1% pre-bell after the company presented six concept cars ahead of the Paris Motor Show, among more than 60 vehicles the automotive giant exhibited at the weeklong event. CNBC reported that the carmaker's Chief Executive Antonio Filosa has called on Europe to provide more incentives for carmakers to build vehicles in the region as Chinese companies increase their share of the European car market.

Health Care

The State Street Health Care Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLV) advanced 0.4%, the Vanguard Health Care Index Fund (VHT) was flat, and the iShares US Healthcare ETF (IYH) was inactive. The iShares Biotechnology ETF (IBB) was 0.1% higher

Humana (HUM) stock was up more than 16% premarket after DataMeds AI (MEDS) said its Helomics subsidiary received a Medicaid coverage determination from Humana for its ChemoFx test in gynecologic cancers.

Commodities

Front-month US West Texas Intermediate crude oil advanced 2% to $93.81 per barrel on the New York Mercantile Exchange. Natural gas was down 3.6% to $3.11 per 1 million British Thermal Units. The United States Oil Fund (USO) increased by 2.5%, while the United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was 2.9% lower.

Gold futures for November retreated by 0.7% to $4,189.20 an ounce on the Comex. Silver futures lost 0.2% to $60.95 an ounce. SPDR Gold Shares (GLD) was down 0.7%, and the iShares Silver Trust (SLV) declined 0.3%.
